commits.summary: prune_workspaces.py: delete jj workspaces only once nothing in them can be lost
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/prune_workspaces.py considers every workspace but the default: those jj lists and the directories of forgotten ones (siblings REPO-* whose .jj/repo points here). It reports by default and deletes only with --delete. A workspace is clear when: no process has its cwd or a file open inside it, and no unfinished loop owns it (a stream workspace NAME-STREAM while llm-dlc/loops/NAME.md's status is neither done nor blocked); every commit of ::WS@ outside ::INTO (the default workspace's @-, or --into) is empty and undescribed; and every file, tracked, untracked or gitignored, is recoverable. That means its exact content is a blob reachable from INTO, or a file anywhere in the default workspace (hashed only on a size match, so its 12 GB verification/.state costs a walk), or it lies in a gitignored build-output directory (target/, build/, ...). It reads file contents, so edits jj never snapshotted count. A .git pointer file jj 0.47 writes is metadata; a .git directory blocks. --archive DIR copies would-be-lost files out and verifies each copy. Deletion re-checks use, forgets a listed workspace, removes the directory and runs git worktree prune. Claude Code transcripts under ~/.claude/projects are left alone.

Verified by test_prune_workspaces.py, 12 cases on throwaway colocated jj repos: merged and deleted; an unmerged commit, an unsnapshotted edit, a unique gitignored .env (and --archive keeping it), a tracked dir named build, a forgotten dir with a unique file, a process inside, a .git directory, and an unfinished loop's workspace all block; a run record copied into the default under another name and ignored target/ are clear. A report-only run here (13 s) finds 3 of 13 clear (the engine-priorities leftovers examples, jbmc, native). The four cleanup-* are kept while cleanup.md waits on jobs. Blocked: the foundations streams' gitignored run records in loop-summaries/ (alignment, heap, observations, summaries), three trace logs only in the foundations directory, and the integration directory's merge files. Nothing was deleted.

commits.summary: prune_workspaces.py only reports, and prints the delete command for a person to run
commits.body:
Without --delete the script only reports whether each workspace is safe to delete, and ends with the exact command that deletes the safe ones. Where a workspace is blocked only by files found nowhere else, it also prints the --archive DIR form. --delete now takes the workspaces by name and refuses unless a person is at a terminal, the check sync.py's allow approve uses: stdin and stdout are terminals, and CLAUDECODE is unset. It checks the named workspaces again, lists the safe ones and asks the person to type "delete" before forgetting and removing any. --archive writes, so it goes with --delete only.

Verified by test_prune_workspaces.py, now 14 cases. The deleting ones run main() with the terminal check and the prompt patched. New: the report prints the command and deletes nothing; --delete is refused in an agent's shell; --delete needs names; a wrong answer deletes nothing; --archive without --delete is a usage error. On this repo the report prints python3 llm-dlc/tools/prune_workspaces.py --delete examples jbmc native, and the same --delete run from this session was refused, with ../in-the-loop-native still in place.

commits.summary: An interrupted push starts no other upload, and the integration scripts run sync.py's run-record and performance suites
commits.body:
test_performance.py's test_an_interrupted_push_keeps_the_urls_it_verified failed 2 times in 3 under CPU load (40 busy loops on vm-1's 28 CPUs), with 5 puts where at most 4 may happen: once a worker took the interrupt, it was free at once and started the next queued log before cmd_upload's finally cancelled the pool. A real Ctrl-C, with a wrangler that dies of it, has the same window. sync.py's Uploader now has a stop flag: a KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit in a worker sets it, cmd_upload sets it first thing when it is left early, and each log checks it before starting and again before its put, raising UploadStopped (not counted as a failure; the interrupt itself still propagates). A put already running finishes and is kept, as before. Reproducer: test_after_an_interrupt_in_a_worker_no_other_put_starts, which failed on the old code (the second log was put after the interrupt) and passes now. Under the same load the whole suite passed 3 times in 3 (103 tests), and every llm-dlc/tools test suite passes.

cleanup-integration.sh now runs test_runs.py and test_performance.py beside test_review.py, as the cleanup loop's for-review list asked. application-core-integration.sh, for the next streams loop (not launched), ran only build.py's Python suite; it now runs sync.py's review, run-record and performance suites too, and application-core.md's list of what TESTS FAILED covers says so.

commits.summary: collect keeps a changes.diff over jj's 1 MiB limit gzipped, or as a summary of the files it changes, for VF-020
commits.body:
jj leaves a new file over snapshot.max-new-file-size (1 MiB) out of every commit, so a large changes.diff never reached the repository. As the user decided, the limit stays and collect fits the diff under it. verification/pipeline.py's keep_diff copies changes.diff as it is when it fits, else writes changes.diff.gz, else changes.stat (each file the diff changes, with lines added and removed, and the diff's size). result.json's changesDiff names the file kept, and collected.changesDiff records the original size and how it was kept; result.schema.json and the README's table describe both. Reproducer: test_pipeline.py's test_a_diff_over_the_commit_limit_is_kept_gzipped_or_as_a_summary, with a 60-file compressible job and a 20-file random one. It failed on the old pipeline.py, which copied each diff as it was, and passes now. The whole suite (28 tests) passes and pipeline.py validate finds 0 problems.

verification/findings.md, VF-020: the fix is recorded, and a mistake in the entry is corrected. Both diffs it named are in fact committed (1,234,232 bytes in pkuvkyln, 1,359,746 bytes in rzmrlklw, both pushed); how they got past the limit is not known. The entry stays open until the next collect of a diff over 1 MiB leaves jj st with no refused file.

commits.summary: The own checker's search for a smaller witness is bounded by work, not time, so the witness is the same on every machine (verification pending)
commits.body: After the first violation, check() in lib/src/bmc/mod.rs searches the remaining paths for one that fails in an earlier stage. It used to stop at as long again as the first violation took, at least a second, so a slower or loaded machine could stop it sooner and report another witness (the verdict was the same either way). This was the last clock dependency in the own checker after VF-010, listed for review by the cleanup loop. The search now stops at as much solver work again as the first violation took (conflicts, at least PROBE_CONFLICTS, 10,000) and as many paths again (at least WITNESS_PATHS, 64): the loop checks the budget before each path, and solve() gives each call only the work left. A solver with no conflict limit keeps the time rule. lib/README.md says so.

commits.summary: The foundations streams' four run records published, and run-streams.sh copies a stream's records into the default workspace itself
commits.body:
feature-loop.sh writes a run's record in llm-dlc/loop-summaries/ of the workspace it runs in, and sync.py publishes only the default workspace's (VF-013). A stream's records were to be copied in when the streams were merged, but nothing did it: the cleanup loop copied its streams' records by hand, and the foundations streams' four (2026-11-07-040118-foundations-alignment, -heap, -observations and -summaries, sessions 11f93b59, 750c8a36, e65240e3 and be22079e) were left only in the forgotten workspaces ../in-the-loop-alignment, -heap, -observations and -summaries, never published. They are copied in, unchanged, and this commit publishes them under their sessions' traces. Before that, each redacted copy was scanned with sync.py's Redactor: no leak, nothing to review, no home path. The originals stay where they were.

So that a later stream's records aren't left behind, llm-dlc/tools/run_records.py collect STREAM DEFAULT copies a workspace's run records into the default workspace: only feature-loop records (not integration reports), a copy replaced only by the record it is a start of (records only grow; one that diverged is left and reported), each written atomically. run-streams.sh calls it at its start (records from an interrupted run), after each of a stream's runs (an interrupted one too), and before the merge, whose commit publishes them. test_runs.py's 5 new tests cover it (they errored before run_records.py existed), and the shell function was run against made-up workspaces: one copy, then nothing on a second call or from the default workspace itself. Run over every workspace directory on disk, it found nothing else missing. test_runs (13), test_streams_status, test_review and test_performance pass. sync.py's comment, llm-dlc/README.md and specification.md say how the records come in.

commits.summary: Stub reachability, step 1: an experiment job that has JBMC's solver decide whether VF-015's proof enters the String.format stub (verification pending)
commits.body:
llm-dlc/loops/stub-reachability.md's step 1. The gap preflight counts a stub as entered when JBMC's symbolic execution alone keeps a step of it. For VF-015's proof (prove Hex#toDigit --assume 'ch == 1632' on commons-codec's old Hex), that counts String.format(String, Object[]) as entered on toDigit's exception path, which the assumption makes infeasible. The new verification/triage/stub-reachability.sh reruns that proof unchanged, with JBMC behind a wrapper that records each command and its time. On the proof's harness and command it then tries two methods. (A) --cover location in place of --unwinding-assertions, reading the goals of DecoderException's constructor, of the stub and of toDigit, and once more with --property on one goal. (B) The proof as given, with a rewritten DecoderException whose String.format call first calls a probe that fails an assertion of its own (throw new AssertionError(), as GapIntrinsics.open). Both also run on a control, the same prove without --assume, where the call is reachable. The job's description gives the outcome each method is expected to have.

Checked inline: the script's syntax, its argv rewriting on made-up commands, and its recording wrapper with echo in place of JBMC. No JBMC was run. The brief's Progress records why the probe is a rewritten caller and not a rewritten goto program: jbmc 6.11 can't write a goto binary for goto-instrument. jbmc --help lists --cover only in --unwinding-assertions' line, so whether --cover is accepted is for the job to show.

Verification pending: job 20261107-233000-stub-reachability-step-1-can-jbmc-s-solv (verification/jobs/). Step 2, choosing the method, waits on its result.

commits.summary: application-core: the user's decisions settled, and VF-015 brought in scope as Phase 0's step 7
commits.body:
The user settled the brief's six proposed decisions as drafted: the four streams as scoped, with optional work never blocking a row; verification with the pipeline; one writer for shared files; Phase 0 in the planning session; 4 GB per stream and about 24 GB for the runner; claude-opus-5-5 at high effort. They added a seventh: VF-015 is in scope. The stub-reachability loop's timebox deferred VF-015 to a person on 2026-11-08, after finding its cause: the equivalence harness's call handlers (harness::EXCEPTIONS) catch only unchecked exceptions and Error, so commons-codec's checked DecoderException leaves EquivalenceHarness.check uncaught, and no equivalence over a method that throws a checked exception can be verified.

It goes in Phase 0, not a stream: the fix is in harness/, the objects stream's file; the environment stream's E2 (modelled failures, catch and propagation) needs it; and it is small. Step 7 has a reproducer first. The handlers then catch each class in either version's throws clause, then java.lang.Exception, comparing by class, and a checked exception that only one version throws is refuted. The closing job is VF-015's resubmitted with step 4 made stricter: the change must be found with its witness replayed, where test $? -eq 1 also accepted 'cannot be verified'. It has no timebox attempt left, so a failure goes back to the user. The starting-point table, prerequisites 1 and 5, Phase 0's Done-when row and Progress are updated, and E2's brief points at step 7. The status stays blocked on Phase 0.
